rows.raw: {"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[0]","value":"Limit correction to a maximum of 10 mEq/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mEq/L per 24 hours thereafter; use an 8 mEq/L/24h ceiling in patients at high risk for osmotic demyelination"},{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[1]","value":"Severe symptoms (seizures, obtundation) warrant 3% hypertonic saline as a 150 mL bolus over 20 minutes, repeated until serum Na rises ~5 mEq/L or symptoms resolve"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Urine osmolality <100 mOsm/kg indicates appropriately suppressed ADH (primary polydipsia, low solute intake); >100 mOsm/kg implies ongoing ADH action"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Cap correction at 10 mEq/L in the first 24 hours (8 mEq/L if high ODS risk), and use hypertonic saline boluses only for severe symptoms"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"High ODS risk: chronic hyponatremia, Na <105, alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, advanced liver disease, hypokalemia"}]}

{"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[1]","value":"Start dapagliflozin 10 mg daily (or empagliflozin 10 mg daily) irrespective of diabetes status"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist is a pillar, not an add-on: start when K <5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >=30 mL/min/1.73 m2"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Loop diuretics relieve congestion but confer no mortality benefit and do not substitute for a pillar"},{"op":"append","path":"sections","value":{"heading":"Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism","minutes":"2-3 min","points":["Aldosterone drives sodium retention, potassium and magnesium wasting, and myocardial fibrosis independent of ACEi/ARB/ARNI therapy","Initiate spironolactone 12.5-25 mg daily or eplerenone 25 mg daily when K <5.0 mEq/L and eGFR >=30 mL/min/1.73 m2, titrating spironolactone to 25-50 mg or eplerenone to 50 mg daily","Recheck potassium and creatinine within 1 week of starting or uptitrating, again at ~4 weeks, then periodically; hold or reduce if K >5.5 mEq/L","Eplerenone is preferred when gynecomastia or breast tenderness limits spironolactone"],"mechanism":"Blocking aldosterone at the mineralocorticoid receptor reduces fibrosis, hypokalemia-driven arrhythmia, and adverse remodeling","teaching_pearl":"Most MRA discontinuation is driven by inadequate monitoring rather than true intolerance","board_tip":"Avoid concurrent potassium supplements and NSAIDs; RALES showed a mortality benefit with spironolactone in NYHA III-IV HFrEF"}}]}

{"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"guideline_sources[1]","value":"2021 Universal Definition and Classification of Heart Failure (ESC/HFA/HFSA/JHFS consensus)"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"HFrEF receives all four GDMT pillars; HFmrEF and HFpEF are managed with SGLT2 inhibitors plus diuretics for congestion"},{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].board_tip","value":"HFimpEF requires all three: a documented baseline EF of 40% or less, an absolute increase of at least 10 points, and a second measurement above 40%"},{"op":"append","path":"sections","value":{"heading":"How classification changes management","minutes":"3-4 min","points":["HFrEF (EF <=40%): all four pillars - ARNI (or ACEi/ARB if ARNI not tolerated), an evidence-based beta blocker (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol), an MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone), and an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin)","HFmrEF and HFpEF: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended, plus diuretics titrated to congestion; MRA and ARNI carry weaker support and are reasonable in selected patients, with benefit greatest at the lower end of the EF range","Obesity-related HFpEF: weight loss with semaglutide or tirzepatide improves symptoms and functional capacity","HFimpEF: continue the same GDMT that produced the improvement - do not de-escalate on the basis of a normalized EF"],"mechanism":"Neurohormonal blockade and SGLT2 inhibition drive reverse remodeling; the survival benefit is largest as EF falls","teaching_pearl":"Classify first, then prescribe - the EF category tells you which trial population your patient belongs to","board_tip":"Check potassium and renal function before and after starting an MRA; avoid initiation if K+ is above 5.0 mEq/L or eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2"}}]}

{"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[1]","value":"Chronic azithromycin reduces exacerbation frequency in selected patients, preferentially former smokers [2]"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days is standard for an exacerbation; no taper needed (REDUCE trial)"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"NIV is first-line for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure (pH <=7.35 with PaCO2 >45 mmHg) and reduces intubation and mortality"}]}

{"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"sections[0].points[2]","value":"Check a potassium (and ideally a point-of-care K) before starting insulin; give fluids first and hold insulin until K is >3.3 mEq/L, then run a fixed-rate infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr without a bolus"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr with no bolus needed; do not start it if K is <3.3 mEq/L until potassium is replaced"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Add dextrose to the fluids when glucose falls below 200 mg/dL so the insulin infusion can continue until the gap closes"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Overlap the infusion with subcutaneous basal insulin by 1-2 hours before stopping it to prevent rebound ketoacidosis"},{"op":"append","path":"sections","value":{"heading":"Endpoints and transition off the drip","minutes":"2-3 min","points":["Glucose corrects faster than ketosis - add dextrose-containing fluid at glucose <200 mg/dL and keep insulin running","Resolution requires two of: anion gap <=12, bicarbonate >=15 mEq/L, venous pH >7.3 - not simply a normal glucose","Give subcutaneous basal insulin 1-2 hours before stopping the infusion to avoid rebound ketosis","Bicarbonate is not routinely given; reserve consideration for pH <6.9, and treat any precipitant (infection, ischemia, missed insulin, drug)"],"mechanism":"Insulin suppresses lipolysis and ketogenesis; the drip must continue past glucose normalization until ketone production stops","teaching_pearl":"You are treating the gap, not the glucose","board_tip":"Beta-hydroxybutyrate, not urine ketones, tracks resolution because nitroprusside assays detect acetoacetate and may appear to worsen with treatment"}}]}

{"verdict":"corrected","patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[0]","value":"Limit correction to 10 mEq/L in the first 24 hours (8 mEq/L in high-risk patients) and no more than 8 mEq/L per 24 hours thereafter [1]"},{"op":"replace","path":"sections[1].points[1]","value":"Severe symptoms (seizure, coma) warrant 3% hypertonic saline 100-150 mL IV over ~20 min, repeated until symptoms improve or Na rises ~5 mEq/L [1]"},{"op":"append","path":"sections[1].points","value":"Chronic SIADH: fluid restriction (<800-1000 mL/day) first; if inadequate add oral salt tablets plus a low-dose loop diuretic or urea 0.25-0.5 g/kg/day; the 2014 European guideline advises against vaptans and demeclocycline for this indication [1]"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Urine sodium plus volume assessment separates SIADH (euvolemic, Una >30 mEq/L) from hypovolemic hyponatremia (Una <30 mEq/L), while low Uosm (<100 mOsm/kg) points to primary polydipsia or beer potomania"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Severe symptoms (seizure, coma) demand hypertonic saline boluses immediately, regardless of how chronic the hyponatremia appears"},{"op":"append","path":"summary_points","value":"Treat the cause: fluid restriction for SIADH, isotonic saline for hypovolemia, and diuresis with water restriction for heart failure or cirrhosis"}]}

no washout is needed coming off an ARB"},{"op":"append","path":"sections","value":{"heading":"Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism","minutes":"2-3 min","points":["Aldosterone drives myocardial and vascular fibrosis, sodium retention, and potassium/magnesium wasting beyond what ACEi/ARB blockade suppresses","Spironolactone 12.5-25 mg daily titrated to 25-50 mg daily, or eplerenone 25 mg daily titrated to 50 mg daily, for NYHA class II-IV HFrEF","Initiate only if K <5.0 mEq/L and eGFR at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m2; both amplify hyperkalemia risk"}},{"op":"append","path":"sections","value":{"heading":"Sequencing, titration, and monitoring","minutes":"3-4 min","points":["Get all four classes on board at low doses within weeks rather than maximizing one agent before starting the next","Target doses: sacubitril-valsartan 97/103 mg twice daily, carvedilol 25 mg twice daily (50 mg twice daily if over 85 kg), metoprolol succinate 200 mg daily, bisoprolol 10 mg daily","Double doses at roughly 2-week intervals as blood pressure, renal function, and volume status allow","Do not start or up-titrate a beta blocker during decompensation with active volume overload or low output; do start once the patient is euvolemic and off inotropes","Reassess LVEF after at least 3 months of optimized therapy before deciding on ICD or CRT"],"mechanism":"Layered blockade of complementary pathways produces additive mortality reduction","teaching_pearl":"Asymptomatic modest creatinine rise and mild hypotension are expected, not reasons to abandon a pillar","board_tip":"Loop diuretics relieve congestion but have no proven mortality benefit and are not one of the pillars"}}]}
